solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Union Jack used by a religious rite

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
unction is the sacramental anointing with oil

explanation.surface: The national flag is being flown at a church ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union Jack' reads as the flag, but 'Union' is the definition and 'Jack' gives only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction is a joining point, as where roads or railway lines meet, so it is a union of routes.

clue.text: Pair I arrested by taking advantage of rebellion

indicators.note: something arrested is held in custody, so these letters are held inside the others

parts.note: using someone is taking advantage of them

explanation.surface: Two rebels are detained by opportunists during a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular revolt against authority is a rising of the people against their rulers, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: In court, deceives with one fabrication

parts.note: to con someone is to swindle or deceive them
I is the Roman numeral for one
a story is a lie, something made up

explanation.surface: A witness in court is lying through an invented tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'with' are link words; 'court' is the definition, not the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A consistory is an ecclesiastical tribunal, such as the assembly of cardinals or a bishop's church court.

clue.text: Daring to poke right inside lip

indicators.note: to poke something in is to push it into a gap, here into the other word
this places the abbreviation within the cheeky word

parts.note: lip is cheek or insolence, which is impudence

explanation.surface: Someone dares to jab a finger into a person's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to poke ... inside' puts R into IMPUDENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashness or reckless boldness is a lack of prudence, so daring as a noun fits the word for foolhardiness.

clue.text: In Nanny's case anything is bad

indicators.note: the word for anything goes in, sitting between the two outer letters
a case is the outside container, so only the outer letters of the nanny are used

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: As far as the nursemaid is concerned, every single thing is naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: The case of 'Nanny' is its outside letters N and Y; AUGHT goes in between them. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is called naughty, the usual nursery synonym for misbehaving.

clue.text: Royal address that may be turned over

indicators.note: the form of address reads the same when turned round end to end

parts.note: the short form of madam used to a queen, which the setter reuses as the palindrome itself

explanation.surface: A grand speech by a monarch might be overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so turning it over leaves it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen is addressed in speech as 'Ma'am' after the first 'Your Majesty', so it is the royal form of address.

clue.text: Spin and its advantage

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of putting a spin on things
'its' means belonging to it, which can be said 'of it'

explanation.surface: Political spin and the benefit it brings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' is expanded to 'of it'; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or benefit, so to profit from something is to gain advantage from it.

clue.text: Age concealed by fat old artist

indicators.note: something concealed by another thing is hidden within it

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
an eon is a vast age

explanation.surface: An elderly overweight painter hides his true years.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Are you wearing a tie? So dine perhaps

indicators.note: a word wearing another has it around it, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: a lace is a cord used to tie a shoe
'art' is the archaic form of 'are' with 'thou', so 'thou art' means you are

explanation.surface: A dress-code query before a dinner out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you' is the archaic 'thou art'. 'So dine perhaps' describes a way of eating: choosing dishes separately from the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering from the menu item by item rather than a set meal is one way of dining, hence 'so dine'.

clue.text: Heartlessly congratulate oneself, having raised contract

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to preen oneself is to be self-congratulatory
up means raised, lifted

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly smug about a deal they have hiked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes the middle E of PREEN, leaving PREN; 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenuptial agreement is a contract signed before marriage to settle property in a divorce.

clue.text: Poor kid runs one more time to keep warmer

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the warmer is held inside

parts.note: again means once more
a muff is a tube of fur used to keep the hands warm

explanation.surface: A poor child runs again to stay warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy child in ragged clothes, a poor urchin.

clue.text: Unfairness of twice concealing answer

indicators.note: a word concealing another hides it inside

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: An unfair process hides the answer twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts A inside BIS; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is prejudice or partiality, which is a form of unfairness.

clue.text: It's so dull, go back on the booze?

definitions.meaning: the simile 'as dull as ...' means very boring
to abandon water is to give up the drink of the sober and so return to alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller wonders whether to start drinking again.
explanation.walkthrough: To ditch is to abandon: ditching water means turning back to alcohol. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'as dull as ditchwater' makes stagnant water the byword for tedium.

clue.text: Payment not initially for one man-hour worked

indicators.note: letters worked are kneaded into a new shape
the first letter of the word for is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wage paid for an hour's labour by one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' leaves OR from 'for'; with I and MANHOUR, 'worked' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorarium is a fee paid for professional services nominally given free, such as a guest lecture.

clue.text: Personal interest doing extra badly

indicators.note: doing something badly messes it up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone does additional work poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an axe to grind is the idiom for a private motive or selfish stake in an issue.

clue.text: Unable to launch Silver Bullet

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a single bullet or cartridge

explanation.surface: The silver bullet, the magic fix, cannot get started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver Bullet' looks like one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the shore or shallows is aground and so cannot be launched or floated off.

clue.text: Palace regularly fail poor player needing support

indicators.note: regular letters are every other one, here the second and fourth

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A weak performer keeps failing and needs a crutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the famous Moorish palace and fortress in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: One may rage, having to assume refusal

parts.note: to infer is to deduce or assume
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry at being expected to take a rebuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One may rage' looks like an angry person; it is a fire. 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing fire rages out of control, and an inferno is exactly such a fierce blaze.

clue.text: Unbaptised male wrong in the head

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the headland word

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a promontory jutting into the sea

indicators.note: wrong letters are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A man without baptism is mentally unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the head' is a headland, not the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening confers a name, so someone unbaptised can be said to have no name.

clue.text: Girl, one heading for church, keeping good time

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: a bride makes her way to church on her wedding day

explanation.surface: A young woman on her way to church is punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts G inside BRIDE, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget is a female first name, given here as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Tearaway hotly disputed mistake

indicators.note: something disputed is argued over and thrown about, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A wild youth's blunder is fiercely argued about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputed' rearranges HOTLY into HOLYT.
explanation.definitionFit: An unruly, mischievous child is called a holy terror, which is what a reckless tearaway is.

clue.text: Fluky to lose king, capturing a knight back? Madness

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the other piece is held inside
losing a piece means it is taken away

parts.note: a fluky win is a lucky one
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: back means the pieces run in the reverse direction

parts.note: N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess game: losing a king while taking a knight would be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' removes K from LUCKY to give LUCY; 'back' turns A N into NA; 'capturing' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is insanity, an old word tied to the moon's supposed effect on the mind.

clue.text: Scientific units on official business

definitions.meaning: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance
printed on British government post, the initials stand for On Her Majesty's Service

explanation.walkthrough: British government letters were franked with the initials of On Her Majesty's Service, meaning official business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohms measure electrical resistance; the initials mark official crown correspondence.

clue.text: Fear to interrupt child speaking? I know what you're thinking

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this word goes inside
speaking signals that the word for child is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a minor is a child in law
dread is fear

explanation.surface: A parent's fear breaks in as a child talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' means the word for a child is heard, and its same-sounding twin, a coal digger, is spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase of a telepath, who claims to know others' thoughts, stands for the performer.

clue.text: Spirit overcome by melancholy

indicators.note: a word overcome by another is swallowed up and lies within it

explanation.surface: A person's vitality is crushed by sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is vigour, dash and enthusiasm, the sense of spirit as liveliness.

clue.text: One picks up plants

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an economy that picks up rises, improving

explanation.surface: Someone gathers flowers from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plants' looks like a verb object of 'picks up'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowering garden plants with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Hold race around town

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A town stages a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCHDALE is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochdale is a mill town in north-west England, birthplace of the co-operative movement.

clue.text: Man that is most like a mouse

parts.note: Tim is a man's name
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A man who is the most mouse-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are proverbially shy, so the most mouse-like person is the shyest of all.
